Chapter 13: Vision for a Just Society
You know, it's so easy to get caught up in the struggle—to focus on everything that's broken and all the things that still need fixing.
But the work of antiracism is about more than just fighting what's wrong. It's really about imagining what's possible. What if justice wasn’t the rare exception, but simply the way things are?
Picture this for a moment. A city where every child has real access to a great education. Where neighborhoods feel safe and welcoming—where differences aren’t something to be feared, but something to be celebrated.
Or think about our workplaces. What if everyone truly had a fair shot? Imagine policies designed to lift up people who've been left behind, instead of leaving them out.
Most of us don’t realize just how powerful having a vision can be. It gives us direction, inspires hope, and brings people together. Without a vision, this work can start to feel endless—and those obstacles? They can seem way too big to overcome.
But here’s the thing. Once people dare to dream, it becomes clear that real change is possible. It starts with small steps—a new policy here, a new relationship there, maybe even just a new way of thinking.
Over time, those little steps build up. They create momentum and open up new possibilities.
A just society isn’t just some fantasy. It’s built, day by day, through the choices we make and the actions we take. It takes courage, persistence, and a willingness to keep moving, even when the path ahead isn’t totally clear.
The work isn’t finished—and honestly, it might never be. But every generation gets a chance to move us closer, to leave the world just a little better than they found it.
